● Shell git show HEAD

  Based on my review of the last commit, here are the consistency gaps and observations:

  Consistency Gaps Review

  Code Consistency Issues:

  1. Magic Number Inconsistency:
    - arbSign(13) used in arbitration.js line 211, but arbSign(12) used in conversation_view.js line 828
    - arbSign(14) used in arbitration.js line 714, but arbSign(13) used in line 211
    - arbSign(11) changed to arbSign(13) in some places but not all

  2. CSS Comment Misalignment:
    - The comment at line 3099: /* A pane sitting on a permission prompt... */ describes the .arb-say-who.warn class, but this
  class only affects the "who is working" pill, not the whole tray's ability to fix issues

  3. CSS Structure Inconsistency:
    - .arb-strip > * rule at line 2983 removes pointer-events: auto; but adds it to .arb-strip instead - this creates a potential
  accessibility issue as all children lose pointer events
    - The comment at line 2979 says "The tray itself takes taps now" but the implementation affects all children

  Visual/Typography Issues:

  4. Font Size Inconsistency:
    - .arb-say-who uses font-size: 0.6rem (very small)
    - .arb-say-note uses font-size: calc(var(--term-font, 13px) * 0.72) - these may create readability issues

  5. Spacing Issues:
    - .arb-say has padding: 0 2px 1px - asymmetric padding
    - .arb-say-note has padding: 1px 3px - very minimal padding for text content

  Semantic/Architecture Issues:

  6. Comment vs Implementation Mismatch:
    - The commit message says "one tray for all four rows" but the CSS structure shows:
      - .arb-strip (the main container with blur effect)
      - .arb-say (inner container)
      - Multiple nested elements - not clearly "four rows"

  7. Accessibility Concern:
    - Removing pointer-events: auto from .arb-strip > * could make interactive elements inside the strip non-functional for users
  with certain assistive technologies

  Test Inconsistency:

  8. Test Expectation Change:
    - Tests now expect no openTerminal calls when pane is working, but this removes direct navigation to specific panes - users now
  have to navigate through roster

  Positive Aspects:

  - Good semantic HTML structure
  - Consistent use of CSS custom properties (--red, --orange, --green)
  - Clear separation of concerns in the arbitration UI
  - Responsive design considerations (wrapping text, growing tray)

  Recommendations:

  1. Standardize arbSign() sizes throughout the codebase
  2. Review pointer-events strategy for accessibility
  3. Consider font size hierarchy for better readability
  4. Add more specific CSS comments that match the actual implementation
  5. Ensure test coverage reflects the new navigation pattern (through roster vs direct pane links)

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  In one short paragraph and with no tools or commands at all, explain what a git rebase does.

  Git rebase rewrites your branch's commit history by moving it to start from a newer point on another branch, essentially
  replaying your commits on top of the target branch. This creates a linear history without merge commits, making the project
  timeline cleaner and easier to follow, but it alters commit hashes so it should only be done on local branches that haven't been
  shared with others.

▸ Credits: 0.15 • Time: 5s
